import re def get_html_tags(html_input: str) -> list[str]: """ Extract all HTML tags from the provided string. Parameters ---------- html_input : str A string containing HTML content. Returns ------- list[str] A list of tag strings found in the input. The tags include opening, closing, and self‑closing forms (e.g.,
,

, ). The function is tolerant of malformed markup and will not raise an exception for ordinary inputs. Notes ----- The regular expression used is intentionally simple and efficient, avoiding catastrophic backtracking by employing a non‑greedy match (`?`) and limiting the character set for tag names to alphanumerics. """ # Pattern explanation: # <\s* : match the opening '<' followed by optional whitespace # /? : optionally match a '/' for closing tags # \s* : optional whitespace after the '/' # [a-zA-Z0-9]+ : tag name (alphanumeric only) # [^>]*? : any characters except '>' lazily (attributes, etc.) # > : closing '>' tag_pattern = re.compile(r'<\s*/?\s*[a-zA-Z0-9]+[^>]*?>', re.IGNORECASE) # Find all non‑overlapping matches tags = tag_pattern.findall(html_input) return tags
